title: Alandspannkaka (Aland oven pancake with semolina and cardamom)

ingredients.name: prune jam or stewed prunes and whipped cream to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F) and butter a 20 x 30 cm baking dish.
Bring the milk to a gentle boil in a saucepan, then whisk in the semolina and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Remove from the heat and let the porridge cool for 10 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the sugar, cardamom and salt, then stir them into the semolina mixture.
Pour the batter into the dish and bake for 30 to 40 minutes until set and golden brown on top.
Cut into squares and serve warm or cold with prune jam and whipped cream.

title: Joulutorttu (Finnish Christmas plum jam pinwheel pastries)
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Cut the puff pastry into 9 equal squares.
Make a cut from each corner of the square towards the centre, stopping about 1 cm from the middle.
Spoon about a teaspoon of jam into the middle of each square.
Fold alternate corners to the centre to make a pinwheel and press down lightly so they stick.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until puffed and golden.
Cool slightly and dust with icing sugar if you like.

title: Kalakukko (Finnish fish and pork baked inside a rye crust)

ingredients.name: salt, plus more for the filling
small whole fish fillets (vendace, perch, whitefish or herring), boned
pork belly or streaky bacon, in thin slices

steps: Mix the rye and plain flour with the salt, warm water and melted fat into a firm, workable dough and let it rest for 20 minutes.
Season the fish fillets generously with salt and pepper.
Roll the dough into an oval about 5 mm thick, large enough to fold over the filling.
Lay half of the pork slices down the centre, cover with the fish and place the remaining pork on top.
Fold the dough over the filling, pinching the seams tightly to seal them, and shape into an oval loaf with the seam underneath.
Place on a baking paper-lined tray and bake at 150 C (300 F) for 3 to 4 hours, covering with foil if it browns too much, so that the fish and pork soften and merge.
Brush the hot crust with melted butter, wrap it in a cloth to soften for 20 minutes, then cut into thick slices and serve warm.

title: Karjalanpaisti (Karelian hot pot, slow-baked pork and beef stew)

ingredients.name: boiled potatoes and lingonberry jam to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 160 C (320 F).
Layer the beef, pork, onions and carrots in a lidded casserole dish, scattering the salt, peppercorns, allspice and bay leaves between the layers.
Pour in the water so that it comes about halfway up the meat.
Cover tightly and bake for 3 to 4 hours, without stirring, until the meat is meltingly tender.
Check once towards the end and add a little hot water if the pot looks dry.
Remove the bay leaves and serve with boiled potatoes and lingonberry jam or pickled cucumber.

title: Kesakeitto (Finnish summer vegetable and milk soup)

ingredients.name: chopped dill or parsley and white pepper to taste

steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a large pot and add the potatoes and carrots; simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and beans and cook for 5 minutes more, then add the peas for the last 3 minutes.
In a small pan melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for a minute, then whisk in the milk gradually until smooth and slightly thickened.
Pour the milk mixture into the vegetables and heat gently without boiling hard.
Season with pepper and more salt if needed.
Serve in warm bowls scattered with dill or parsley.

title: Lanttulaatikko (Finnish swede casserole)

ingredients.name: fine dry breadcrumbs, plus 1 tbsp for the dish

steps: Boil the swede in salted water for 25 to 30 minutes until very soft, then drain well.
Mash it smooth, return it to the pot and dry over low heat for a minute.
Soak the breadcrumbs in the cream for 10 minutes.
Mix the mash with the soaked crumbs, egg, syrup, nutmeg and salt.
Grease a baking dish with butter and coat it with a spoonful of breadcrumbs.
Spoon in the mixture, level it and dot with the remaining butter.
Bake at 175 C (350 F) for 60 to 75 minutes until set and golden, and serve as a side with ham.

title: Lihapiirakka (Finnish deep-fried meat and rice pies)
steps: Mix the yeast with the warm milk and sugar, add the flour, salt and butter and knead until smooth; let it rise for 1 hour.
Fry the beef and onion in a dry pan until cooked and any liquid has gone, then mix with the rice, salt and pepper and cool.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into an oval about 12 cm long.
Spoon some filling in the middle of each oval, fold the dough over and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Let the pies rest on a tray, seam side down, for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil to 170 C (340 F) and fry the pies in small batches for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, plain or with mustard.

title: Lohikeitto (Finnish creamy salmon soup)

ingredients.name: salmon fillet, skinned, cut into chunks
fresh dill, salt and pepper to taste

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the leek and onion for 4 to 5 minutes without browning.
Add the stock, potatoes, carrot, allspice and bay leaves and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Pour in the cream and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Add the salmon chunks and poach for 4 to 5 minutes until just opaque; do not boil hard.
Remove the bay leaves, season with salt and pepper and stir in plenty of chopped dill.
Serve hot with rye bread.

title: Lortsy (Finnish half-moon pastries with apple or meat filling)
steps: Mix the yeast with the warm milk and sugar and leave for 10 minutes, then add the flour, salt, butter and egg and knead until smooth; let it rise for an hour.
Cook the grated apple with the filling sugar and cinnamon in a small pan for 5 minutes, until thick; cool.
Roll the dough out 4 mm thick and cut into rounds about 12 cm wide.
Put a spoonful of apple filling on one half of each round, fold the dough over and pinch the edges closed, then crimp with a fork.
Place on a lined tray, brush with beaten yolk and prick the tops with a fork.
Bake at 200 C (400 F) for 15 to 18 minutes until golden brown and serve warm.

title: Makaronilaatikko (Finnish macaroni and minced meat casserole)

ingredients.name: minced beef or beef and pork mix
ketchup or lingonberry jam to serve

steps: Boil the macaroni in salted water for 3 minutes less than the packet says, then drain.
Fry the onion in the butter until soft, add the mince and cook until browned; season with salt and pepper.
Mix the macaroni with the meat in a greased ovenproof dish.
Beat the eggs with the milk and pour the mixture over the macaroni.
Bake at 200 C (400 F) for 35 to 40 minutes until set and lightly golden on top.
Serve with ketchup, lingonberry jam or pickled cucumbers.

title: Maksalaatikko (Finnish liver and rice casserole)

ingredients.name: lingonberry jam and melted butter to serve

steps: Cook the rice in the water and milk, stirring occasionally, for about 20 minutes until it has made a soft porridge; cool it.
Fry the onion in the butter until soft and let cool.
Grind or blend the liver to a coarse paste.
Mix the liver, rice porridge, onion, eggs, syrup, raisins, marjoram and salt together.
Pour the mixture into a buttered baking dish.
Bake at 175 C (350 F) for 60 to 75 minutes until firm and browned on top.
Serve hot or warm, with lingonberry jam and melted butter.

title: Munavoi (Finnish egg butter spread)
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until hard, then cool them in cold water and peel them.
Chop the eggs finely with a knife or mash them with a fork.
Mash the soft butter into the eggs until the mixture is spreadable.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in the chives if using.
Serve straight away or chill, as a topping for warm rye flatbread, rieska, Karelian pasties or rye bread.

title: Poronkaristys (Finnish sauteed reindeer, with beef or venison substitute)

ingredients.name: thinly sliced reindeer meat (or venison or beef sirloin as a substitute), partly frozen to ease slicing
mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam to serve

steps: Melt half of the butter in a large heavy frying pan over high heat.
Fry the meat in batches, spreading it thinly in the pan, until just browned on all sides, and set it aside.
Lower the heat, add the remaining butter and cook the onion until soft and golden.
Return the meat to the pan with the crushed allspice, salt and pepper.
Pour in the water or beer, cover and simmer gently for 30 to 45 minutes until tender, adding a little more liquid if it gets dry.
Serve with mashed potatoes, lingonberry jam and pickled cucumber.

title: Pulla (Finnish cardamom braided sweet bread)

ingredients.name: pearl sugar or flaked almonds to top

steps: Mix the yeast with the warm milk and a spoonful of the sugar and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Add the egg, the rest of the sugar, cardamom, salt and about half of the flour and stir to a thick batter.
Add the rest of the flour and knead until the dough is smooth, then knead in the soft butter in pieces until the dough is soft and elastic.
Cover and let it rise for 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into three equal pieces, roll them into ropes and braid, tucking the ends under.
Place on a lined tray, cover and rise for another 30 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with pearl sugar or almonds and bake at 200 C (400 F) for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden.

title: Ronttonen (Kainuu open pies filled with potato and lingonberries)
steps: Mix the rye flour, plain flour, salt, warm water and melted butter into a firm dough and rest for 20 minutes.
Stir the mashed potatoes with the lingonberries and sugar to make the filling.
Heat the oven to 225 C (435 F).
Roll the dough thinly and cut out rounds about 12 cm wide.
Put a spoonful of filling in the middle of each and fold the edges up and over, pleating them so the centre stays open, to make a small cup.
Place on a lined tray and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the crust is firm and the edges slightly browned.
Brush with melted butter and keep under a cloth for a few minutes to soften before serving.

title: Runebergintorttu (Runeberg torte, Finnish almond and raspberry jam cakes)

ingredients.name: icing sugar, mixed with a little water to a thick paste

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F) and grease 8 to 10 muffin or small tall tins.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the egg.
Mix the almonds, crumbs, flour, baking powder and cardamom, and fold into the mixture alternately with the cream and rum.
Spoon the batter into the tins until two-thirds full.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden and risen, then cool in the tins.
Pipe or spoon a ring of icing around the edge of each cake and put a spoonful of raspberry jam into the centre.

title: Sultsina (Karelian rye pancakes filled with semolina porridge)

ingredients.name: melted butter and egg butter or jam to serve

steps: Mix the rye flour, salt, warm water and oil into a smooth dough, cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Bring the milk to a gentle boil, whisk in the semolina and sugar and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick; cool.
Heat the oven to 225 C (435 F).
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a thin round about 15 cm wide.
Spread a layer of semolina porridge over the middle, fold the edges over towards the centre leaving the middle open, and pinch to hold.
Place on a lined tray and bake for 15 minutes until the rye crust is firm and the porridge has a lightly browned top.
Brush with melted butter and serve warm.

title: Uunijuusto (Finnish baked milk pudding, made with ordinary milk)

ingredients.name: cloudberry or other berry jam to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 175 C (350 F) and butter a medium ovenproof dish.
Whisk the eggs with the salt and the sugar, if using.
Whisk in the milk gradually until evenly mixed.
Pour into the dish and place it in a larger tin; pour hot water around it to halfway up.
Bake for about 45 to 60 minutes, until set with a golden surface and a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool slightly and serve warm or cold in slices with berry jam or fresh berries.

title: Vispipuuro (Finnish whipped lingonberry semolina porridge)

ingredients.name: cold milk or cream to serve

steps: Simmer the berries in the water for 10 minutes until they burst.
Strain the liquid through a sieve, pressing out the juice, and discard the skins.
Return the juice to the pan with the sugar and bring to a boil.
Pour in the semolina in a slow stream, whisking constantly, and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Pour the porridge into a large mixing bowl and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Whisk it with an electric whisk for 5 to 10 minutes until pale pink, light and about triple the volume.
Serve straight away, or chilled, with cold milk or cream.
